title: policy-as-data rollout runtime with slice-aware shadow validation
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: Customers need more expressive, auditable rollout controls that are easy to reason about and test. Current rollout definitions are split across CRDs, controllers, and hard-coded heuristics, which makes small policy changes risky. This PR introduces a policy-as-data runtime for rollouts plus a lightweight slice-aware shadow validation pipeline. Goals: (1) let product/platform teams declare rollout intent (traffic schemas, slice predicates, metric gates) as JSON/YAML policies; (2) evaluate policies in a deterministic runtime at decision time; (3) validate candidate model variants by shadowing real0 traffic through slice-specific validators before shifting live traffic; (4) provide explainable rollback oracles with a compact decision trace for audits and post-mortems. Key changes: - rollout-policy-schema: a stable JSON schema and Go validator for declarative rollout policies (routes, slices, gating metrics, thresholds, holdpoints). - policy-runtime: a new policy evaluation layer in the serving control plane that evaluates policies as first-class objects; supports staged evaluation, dry-run, and explain() traces. - slice-validator: shadow pipeline that samples traffic by slice predicates and runs it through candidate model variants; aggregates per-slice success/failure signals and surfaced metrics to Console. - rollback-oracle: composed decision logic that computes whether a policy should trigger an automated rollback based on multi-signal windows (latency, failure-rate, quality-regression) and decay-weighted historical baselines. - telemetry and observability: new per-policy metrics, per-slice histograms, trace annotations, and Console dashboard templates. - e2e tests and an integration harness that simulates multi-slice A/B traffic and failure modes. Backwards compatibility: policies default to a compatibility-mode that translates existing Release/Canary objects into the new schema (opt-in flag on operators). Default rollout behavior remains unchanged until a policy resource is attached to a service. Checklist: - [x] JSON schema and strict validator implemented - [x] Policy runtime + eval API + explain traces - [x] Slice-aware shadow ingest and validation hooks - [x] Rollback oracle with unit tests and integration tests - [x] Console panels and exportable report for audits - [x] Documentation and examples (quickstart policy, common slices) - [x] Migration guide for existing rollout objects Testing: unit tests for schema and runtime (coverage ~82%), integration tests in benchmark-lab harness simulating 3 slices, staging soak with feature flag for 48h. Rollout plan: merge to main behind rollout-policy feature flag; share experimental policy samples with early enterprise customers and operator teams; enable policy attestation in nightly canaries once we gather 72h of shadow validation data. Risks and mitigations: - Increased decision latency: policy runtime is optimized for hot-path evaluation and uses memoization; measured p50 decision time on staging < 1.2ms. - Telemetry overhead: slice sampling is configurable (default 0.5% per slice) and can be throttled. - Policy misconfiguration: strict schema + server-side validation + lint rules in SDKs; Console warns on unsafe thresholds. Related work: builds on prior canary controller efforts (ENG-3180), shadow verifiers, and the rollout-simulation harness (benchmark-lab).

review_conversation: Reviewer Noah Reed: Requested that explain() traces include the evaluated predicate set and the decision timestamp. Also asked for a stress test for policy eval under 10k qps. Author reply: added predicate dump to explain() and added benchmark script (benchmarks/multi_slice_run.yaml). Reviewer Lena Ortiz: asked for clearer migration path and a guarantee that existing canaries are unchanged by default. Author reply: added compatibility translation logic and operator opt-in flag; added docs section. Arjun Mehta: flagged potential risk with rollout-oracle window size and suggested a configurable decay half-life; author updated oracle to accept tuned decay parameter and added unit tests. CI: all checks passed after one flaky lint rerun (flake in Go test - fixed by ordering test seeds). Approvals: Noah Reed approved, Lena Ortiz approved, Arjun Mehta approved. Merge: squash on green by Maya Patel.
release_notes: Introduces a declarative policy-as-data rollout runtime, slice-aware shadow validation pipeline, and an automated rollback oracle. Feature is gated behind 'rollout-policy' feature flag; default behaviour remains unchanged for existing canaries. Provides migration guide and Console audit panels.
notes_for_release_engineering: Enable feature flag off by default. Run integration harness for 72h in staging and collect per-slice metrics. Coordinate with customers enrolled in early policy trials before enabling in production.
hotfix_followups: Add a low-priority item to monitor explain() trace size in high-churn policies (ENG-4299).
testing_summary: Unit coverage: schema/runtime/oracle ~82%. Integration: 3-slice A/B simulation with injected regressions showed rollback-oracle triggered within expected windows. Load: policy eval benchmark at 10k qps with median eval latency 1.0ms, p99 3.8ms. Shadow sampling default set to 0.5% per slice for safety.
notes: This PR intentionally treats policies as data to make rollout behavior auditable and testable. It centralizes decision logic in a single runtime to reduce drift between operator-configured rules and controller heuristics.
